verdict: With 1,007 freeform COMSOL cells, a model trained on COMSOL data alone has nearly caught up (a network on the freeform COMSOL cells: 0.27 GHz, mean of both edges, down from 1.79 GHz with 97 cells); PWE plus correction is still slightly more accurate (0.25 GHz) and needs no freeform COMSOL cells to start (0.36 GHz with none). PWE is the cheap route when COMSOL runs are scarce; with about 1,000 runs of the shapes being designed, COMSOL data alone become a real alternative.
shapeNote: Why the 1,000 new circles did not help the freeform shapes: the PWE error at the upper band edge depends on the shape. PWE's upper edge is 0.40 GHz too high for circles but 0.50 GHz too low for freeform holes. The circles make the correction almost perfect for circles, but they pull its freeform upper edge the wrong way. Lesson: a correction needs COMSOL cells of the shapes being designed.
